Targeted searches for "Our Missing Hearts" with "third-person", "third person", and "narrator" found corroborating reviews from Chicago Review of Books and Winnipeg Free Press; no credible source described sustained first- or second-person base sections.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, moving its focal attention chiefly between Bird and Margaret while retaining the same external narrating position. Numerous Goodreads passages independently show close third-person access through he/she, and the sustained opening extract plus whole-book descriptions agree. The first-person addresses in q07440 and q07459 are local speech or storytelling by Margaret to her child, not autonomous base sections; universal you passages likewise do not establish second person. References to alternating perspectives concern focal characters, not alternating narrative person. No material uncertainty remains.
